event: Elsie wakes in the loft at first light; Cora is still asleep, her hand open in Elsie's.
Asleep, Cora's face has gone soft, her mouth a little open, one black strand loose from her bun.
Elsie lies very still so as not to wake her; she has never once seen Cora asleep.
Tilly is wound round Elsie's back, breathing into her hair; Tamsin snores face-down by the ladder.
Cora's eyes open, very close to Elsie's; for a breath she doesn't move or look away.
Then she sees their hands, goes red to the hair, and sits up so fast she hits a rafter.
Elsie asks if she slept; Cora says yes, and this time it's true, and Elsie says so, delighted.

changes.note: Bond: Cora 48 → 49 (kindness: her hand held all night, and glad she slept)

event: Cora pins the loose strand back into her bun with unsteady fingers, and doesn't meet her eye.
From the loft window the great wheel is turning, slow and steady, and the race below runs clear.
Down on the bank the race's stones stand stacked in a neat wall, the weed coiled beside them.
Bess comes out in her shawl, sees the stacked stones, and puts her floury hand over her mouth.
By the back step the blue bowl sits licked clean and turned upside down on the stone.
Bess says that's how Mam used to find it every morning, and laughs and cries at once.
Elsie hugs her, flour and all; Bess pats her back, hard, the way you'd pat a calf.
Breakfast in the cottage is porridge with cream poured over it, a whole jug, for once.
Tamsin has three bowls; Tilly reads her grave book over hers and drips porridge on a wight.
Bess writes on a scrap of sack paper that the wheel is cleared and the job done, and signs it.
She heaves up a full sack of flour, ground fine, for Agnes Merriweather: her sorry for the grit.
Tamsin swings the sack onto her shoulder without being asked, Margery in her other hand.
At the gate the younger daughter whispers thank you and presses a hot bun into Elsie's hand.
They set off north up the river road beside the Wend, the sun already warm on their backs.
Elsie breaks the bun in two and gives Cora the bigger half; Cora eats it walking, every crumb.

changes.note: Bond: Cora 49 → 50 (kindness: the bigger half of the bun)

event: Elsie knits as she walks; the second glove grows past its cuff, and she starts the thumb.
Cora watches the needles a long while, then asks, very low, if the gloves are for cold hands.
Elsie says they're a surprise, beaming; Cora looks down at her own bare hands and says nothing.
Tilly asks Tamsin if a boggart counts as a grave thing; Tamsin says nothing counts, and laughs.
They come in by the south gate at half past nine, and the city smells of bread and canal water.
At the Honeycomb Tamsin swings the sack onto the counter; Agnes looks at it, then at Elsie.
Elsie tells her the race is clear, and about the cream on the step, and gives her Bess's sorry.
Agnes opens the sack and rubs the flour between finger and thumb; it doesn't squeak.
She says, Good, and nothing more, and wraps four slices of seed cake for them to take.
In the window the honey cakes still sit in their row on the blue plate, dull and sunk, uneaten.
Elsie looks at them a long moment, and says she'll bake fresh ones tonight, in case.
In the guild hall Elsie lays Bess's signed scrap on the clerk's desk; the clerk reads it twice.
The clerk counts out nine silver lanterns, and Tamsin deals them three by three into three palms.

event: Elsie closes her hand on her three lanterns, warm from the clerk's box, and drops them in her purse.
Cora writes it in her ledger, then goes behind the charcoal door to file her sheet.
Elsie buys a pot of tea at the bar for two pips, and a cup of black coffee for two pips more.

changes.note: Elsie buys a pot of tea and Noor's black coffee at the bar, 2 pips each: 4 pips, 215 → 211

event: She carries both across the empty ring to Noor's table, watching her feet the whole way.
Noor watches her come; Elsie shakes the empty chair hard, knocks on its seat, and sits.
It holds; she pours her tea and slides the coffee across, its handle toward Noor's glove.

changes.note: Bond: Noor 3 → 4 (kindness: black coffee, handle to her glove)

event: Elsie asks after the honey cakes; Noor says there were four, and now there are none.
Noor says it flat as a slate, but her mouth goes in at the corner, and she turns her cup.
Elsie claps; the lid hops off the teapot at the clap, rolls round the table, and drops in her lap.
Elsie laughs and puts the lid back; Noor watches her laugh, and this time doesn't look away.
Elsie asks again if Noor will have lunch with her one day; Noor says, Ask me tomorrow.
Elsie says that's nearly a yes; Noor says it's nothing of the kind, and drinks her coffee.
Tilly comes running from the board, braids flying: there's a new F-rank notice, a lost cat.
She reads it: a lost cat called Biscuit, near Ash Lane, small, white, very friendly; two lanterns.
It's signed I. Calderón; Tamsin says two lanterns won't buy Margery a whetstone.
Elsie says somebody's crying over that cat, Pudding taught her that, so that settles it.
Cora comes back from the Wardens' room, sees the name on the notice, and goes very still.
Cora says, flatly, that Ines Calderón is registered with the guild, as Elsie is: a Necromancer.
Tamsin's face falls; Tilly hugs her fat book to her chest and says, at last, a grave thing.
Elsie asks Cora whether a Necromancer can't love her cat; Cora opens her mouth, and shuts it.
Elsie takes the notice to the desk and signs for the party; the clerk stamps it without a word.
At the door Elsie waves; Noor lifts her glove up past her shoulder, and keeps it up.
Ash Lane runs behind the Hall of Naming, narrow and shady, its tall houses leaning together.
The narrowest house is painted black, with a little flap cut low in its door.
Elsie knocks; a long while after, the door opens a crack, and a small pale face looks out.
The girl is tiny and porcelain-pale in black lace, with a sleek black bob and red-rimmed eyes.
Elsie holds up the notice and says they've come about Biscuit, and the girl's dark eyes go wide.
She whispers that she is Ines, and nobody ever takes her notices, and looks past at Cora's coat.
Her hands knot in her lace; she whispers that Biscuit isn't quite an ordinary cat.
Tamsin asks how not ordinary; Ines whispers he's bones, only bones: her kitten, raised again.
Tamsin takes a step back down off the step; Tilly takes a step up, her eyes shining.
Elsie asks if he still purrs; Ines stares at her, and says yes, with no throat to purr with.
Elsie says then he's a cat, and a lost one, and takes Ines's cold little hand: they'll find him.

changes.note: Bond: Ines 0 → 2 (stand: a cat of bones is still a cat, and they'll find him)

event: Ines looks down at her hand in Elsie's, and her pale face goes pink right up into her fringe.
Ines whispers he's been gone three days over the roofs, and he's never been gone past one.
She says he loves warm places best: warm laps, sills in the sun, the step by a bread oven.
They split up: Tamsin and Tilly take the back yards, Elsie, Ines and Cora the lane's gutters.
A washerwoman says a skeleton sat on her wall two nights back, and she screamed the street up.
A boy says something white ran along the gutters toward the lake, rattling like dice in a cup.
Tamsin comes back pale; a pigeon burst out of a yard at her, and she nearly swung Margery at it.
At the end of the lane Elsie stops: the Hall's glass dome blazes in the sun, hot as an oven door.
She says if she were a cat made of bones, that's where she'd want to lie.
Ines looks up at the blazing dome, and puts her hand over her mouth.
In the Hall the priestess who named Elsie sees her and goes pale, and sees Ines and goes paler.
Elsie asks her very nicely if they may go up on the roof for a lost cat; she points to a door.
A narrow stair winds up inside the wall and comes out on the leads round the foot of the dome.
On the far side, on the hot glass in full sun, lies a small white skeleton cat, curled up.
He's up the dome's curve above the gutter, and one hind foot is caught fast in a crack in the lead.
Ines calls him in a whisper; he lifts his little skull and mews, a thin dry sound, and can't come.
Cora says nobody goes out on that glass; it's a long way down to the stones of the hall floor.
Elsie pulls off her boots, says she's the lightest of them, and crawls onto the warm glass.
Cora drops flat on the leads behind her and grips her by the ankle, hard, with both hands.
The glass is hot under her palms; far down through it she sees the silver circle she was named in.
She hums to him without knowing it as she inches close, and he stops struggling to listen.
She works his tiny foot bones out of the crack one by one, the way she worked the mill stones.
Biscuit climbs into the crook of her arm, light as a bundle of twigs, and begins to purr.
The purr buzzes up her arm, warm from the glass, and Elsie laughs out loud on top of the dome.
Cora draws her back by the ankle, hand over hand, until she's on the leads again.
Cora's face is white; she lets go at last and sits back on her heels, breathing as if she ran.
Elsie puts Biscuit into Ines's arms; Ines holds him under her chin and cries without a sound.

changes.note: Bond: Ines 2 → 4 (stand: Elsie crawls out on the dome for Biscuit)

event: Elsie sits down by Cora on the leads and pulls her boots back on; Cora's hands are shaking.
Elsie takes them and says she's all right, look; Cora says, very low, Don't do that again.

changes.note: Bond: Cora 50 → 53 (danger shared: she holds Elsie's ankle on the dome; cap of 5)
Heart 16 → 17 (Devotion: Cora 53% of 21)
Cora Heart 31 → 32 (Devotion: 53% of 21)

event: Elsie says she'd do it for any of them; Cora looks at her, and doesn't say anything to that.
On Ash Lane Ines asks them in, so quietly it's clear she has never asked anyone in.
Her front room is small, full of books and dried flowers, with birdcages hung up, doors open.
Tamsin stays standing by the door, as far from Biscuit as the little room allows.
Biscuit trots straight to her, climbs her boot, and settles purring in her lap when she sits.
Tamsin sits rigid with her hands in the air, and asks in a whisper what she's meant to do.
Elsie says stroke him; Tamsin does, with one finger, and her face goes from horror to wonder.

changes.note: Bond: Tamsin 81 → 84 (held through a fear: Biscuit in her lap)

event: Ines makes tea, but her hands shake on the pot, so Elsie takes it gently and pours for her.
Tilly asks Ines a hundred questions about raising things; Ines answers every one, pleased.
Ines asks Elsie, low, if she is the Enthraller; the whole city talks of her, she says.
Elsie says yes, cheerfully, it's a dreadful name; she asks if Necromancer is a dreadful one too.
Ines says people cross the lane when they see her, and in the square they look at Elsie the same.
Elsie hadn't noticed; she thinks of the silent hall, and the clerk's stopped pen, and goes quiet.
Ines whispers they'll watch her all her life, waiting for her to be what the name says.
Elsie says then they'll be waiting a very long time; Ines looks at her, and very nearly smiles.

changes.note: Bond: Ines 4 → 5 (confidence: the name they wait on; cut to the cap of 5)

event: Cora stands by the window with her ledger open, and her pen doesn't move.
Elsie takes out her notebook and asks Ines what her favourite things are.
Ines says hot milk with honey, the hour before dawn, and Biscuit asleep on her feet.
Elsie writes it down and draws a tiny cat of bones by her name; Ines looks at it a long time.
Ines says she'll tell the guild clerk in the morning that Biscuit's home, so the notice pays.
At the door Elsie hugs her; Ines goes stiff, then still, her face against Elsie's shoulder.
Ines whispers that Elsie may come again, if she likes; Elsie says she will, and means it.
They walk back toward Brightwater Square in the long gold light off the lake.
Tamsin says she had a dead cat in her lap and it purred, and she's going to tell her mum.
Tilly says it's the best day of her whole life, and writes Biscuit down in the back of her book.
At the guild hall doors the hall is shutting for the day, and Cora stops on the top step.
She opens her ledger and shows Elsie the line: Ash Lane. Lost cat, found. Skills used, none.
Elsie squeezes Cora's bare hand and finds it warm for once, and tells her so, delighted.
Cora says she has her report to write; she says it to the doorframe, red to the collar.
Cora goes off along the canal toward Wick Lane; she doesn't look back, and then she does.
Tamsin heads off toward the docks and Tilly toward Pickle Row, both waving till the corner.
In the Honeycomb kitchen after closing Elsie bakes honey cakes with Bess's fine new flour.
She brushes them with the last of the comb and counts twenty, and they come out crackling.
She sets them out on the blue plate in the window, a fresh row, under the red lantern.
Up in the attic she adds Biscuit to Ines's page, and draws a little sun on a dome above him.
She knits by the round window, and the second glove's thumb takes shape between her needles.
She tries the finished glove on her own hand again; its fingers flap at the ends: just right.
She lays the half-glove on the sill beside the finished one, by Moonpenny, nearly a pair.
She tells Moonpenny about the bones that purred, and blows out the candle.
